doc.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023

chapter: Army, Chicago and the new music
title: Apprenticeship in Chicago and lending Dexter Gordon a rubber band
summary: Eddie Buster encouraged his new sound; he describes the apprenticeship environment of Chicago and handing Dexter Gordon a rubber band when a spring broke.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. They were all encouraging me to do that because like back then you had like the apprenticeship and so on, where all you had to do was show someone that you wanted to know something from that you were interested and they would take you on and show you like how to do it you know. And so yeah, yeah, it was that kind of environment like in Chicago you know. And so it was all there in a way you know. The off nights it was local musicians and sessions and stuff, but then on the weekend you’d have the big players up in there. So I recall Dexter Gordon was there playing and you know a spring broke on his horn and he needed a rubber band and I just happened to have a rubber band with me you
know, so I gave him that. I mean I guess the next time I saw Dexter was like when the Art Ensemble went to Europe, so he was there in Copenhagen.
